name: Anglerfish
description: Famous for its glowing lure dangling before toothy jaws. Females dwarf males, which fuse parasitically to share her bloodstream.

name: Vampire Squid
description: Neither true squid nor octopus, it turns its cape inside out when threatened, revealing spiny cirri and photophores along its arms.

name: Giant Isopod
description: A deep-sea cousin of the pill bug, growing to the size of a football. It scavenges whale falls and can fast for years between meals.

name: Comb Jelly
description: Rows of cilia refract light into rainbow pulses as it swims. Unlike jellyfish, it hunts other jellies with a gaping mouth.

name: Barreleye Fish
description: Its transparent, fluid-filled head shields upward-facing tubular eyes. It steals prey from siphonophores without being stung.

name: Portuguese Man o' War
description: Not one animal but a colony: a gas-filled float, feeding polyps, and stinging tentacles that can stretch 30 meters below the surface.

name: Giant Squid
description: The largest invertebrate on Earth, with eyes the size of dinner plates. Elusive until a live specimen was filmed in 2004 off Japan.

name: Dragonfish
description: Produces red bioluminescence invisible to most prey. Its jaws unhinge to swallow animals half its own body length.

name: Sea Angel
description: A translucent, wing-flapping pteropod that hunts shelled sea butterflies. In polar waters its body glows faintly pink.

name: Hatchetfish
description: Silver-sided body with ventral photophores that erase its silhouette from predators below — a strategy called counter-illumination.

name: Yeti Crab
description: Discovered near hydrothermal vents in 2005, its arms are covered in filamentous bacteria it may cultivate for food or detoxification.

name: Siphonophore
description: A chain of specialized clones — some sting, some digest, some swim — that together form one of the longest animals on Earth.
